note: One bend per phrase over a slow minor blues, with the two bend notes ringed on positions 1 and 2, then phrases answered across the crossing on a position-neck with cross. Moves holds any key and 70 to 80 bpm, so the text names the key as a param.

exercise.title: Slow blues, one bend a phrase
exercise.why: A bend held over a slow backing track has time to be heard, so one bend per phrase trains you to aim it and wait on it.

cells.text:
Press Play above to start the backing track: a slow 12-bar blues in {{=key}} minor. The neck below shows positions 1 and 2 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale. Play short phrases from it and put one bend in each: the ringed {{4}} up to {{5}}, or the ringed {{b7}} up to {{1}}. Hold the bend and let the backing track move under it before you go on.
Practice until each bend reaches its note and stays there.

Press Play above to start the backing track again. Play a phrase low in position 1, then answer it with one that takes the crossing: a slide up the G string from the ringed {{4}} to the ringed {{5}}, ending in position 2. Keep the two phrases close, as if one replies to the other.
{{?key}}In another key both positions sit on other frets, and the crossing is still the slide from {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string.
